findings.text: — probe-angle supply is spread across four owners: _supply_declared_probe_angles here (acquisition-address branch, MAST), imas_ambix/data/geometry_adapter.py:165 _b_probes writes angle_deg=NaN unconditionally, imas_ambix/gs/geometry.py:842 load_tables reads angles via load_packaged_signal_map("mast","magnetics"), imas_ambix/spine_bench/transform_*_source.py:266 _supply_probe_orientations joins them again, and imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py:582-601 drops any probe whose poloidal_angle is absent — §6 then adds a fifth (the "description" branch in read_geometry_table that reads the emitted poloidal_angle). The catalogue already carries probe_angle_source ("acquisition-address" for MAST, "description" for DIII-D and JT-60SA, imas_ambix/data/machine_maps/*.json:10) as the one selector, but only the description_reader branch consults it, so the mechanism has no single owner of "where a probe's directed angle comes from". Would change the plan: yes — a plan-changing response is to route every site through the declared probe_angle_source (or say in the plan why the off-route sites must stay separate), since §6 otherwise grows the surface without retiring one. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: consolidating behind the selector already introduced by §4 removes a fifth implementation instead of adding one.

— MAST_TO_COCOS_17_FACTORS hand-maintains a transformation-class factor table (already carrying "pol_angle_like": -1.0 at :438) that duplicates the table nova owns (nova/nova/io/cocos.py:87 TRANSFORMATIONS, reached through imas_ambix/cocos.py:63 canonical_factor), while §6 proposes to add pol_angle_like to nova and says ambix "adds none" without naming this second table. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: no — REASON: the ambix table is consumed only by tests as an agreement check on nova's factors (tests/data/test_cocos_convention.py:179-200), so it is a guard rather than a runtime second owner, and naming it would not force a design change.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3/§7 funnel EQDB through RemoteEddbExtractor and the eddb.py store so transport, niced/module-load, and the pulse-group token and overwrite invariants have one implementation, and §7's SELENE chain is one fetch, one reader, two adapters rather than a second reader.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — probe-angle supply is reimplemented at four pre-existing sites with no single owner, and §6 adds a fifth inline branch rather than routing supply through the probe_angle_source selector the catalogue already carries; census in the FINDING line.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every adding section names the name it retires or states why nothing can be (§3 "retire nothing, because ambix had no remote reader"; §4 "the two store-addressing keys retire nothing"; §6 retires mast_angle_to_canonical, adds measure_convention; §7 retires the three PINNED_* definitions for one table).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and extends the owners it would otherwise fork (imas_ambix/data/signal_map.py load_packaged_signal_map, imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py score_convention, imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py judge_geometry, imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py, imas_ambix/gs/machine_identity.py, imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py + eddb.py, imas_ambix/data/paths.py, imas_ambix/data/description_identity.py), and for each new mechanism states why the existing owner cannot carry it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the tokamap exporter (§2), the EQDB request/record types and grid writer (§7) each state why the existing mechanism cannot be extended, against what they retire or why nothing can be.
